overview: Manage staff training, resident records, and daily tasks in one place. See what needs attention and keep documentation organized for your next survey.
summary: CareBase brings training records, credentials, clearances, resident assessments, incidents, and inspections together. Assign follow-up tasks, monitor deadlines, and export the documentation your surveyor requests.
intro: From the morning med pass to the next survey: explore resident care, training, eMAR, workforce, billing, and the tools that connect them. Start with Core and choose the modules your facility needs.

pillars.title: Prepare for your next survey
pillars.why: Track requirements and due dates under Chapters 2600 and 2800, keep supporting records together, and export a binder for survey review. Missing records stay visible so your team can follow up.

pillars.title: Spend less on required education
pillars.why: Your course library is built and kept current for you by the CareMetric team, including AI-assisted courses based on your own policies. Live-class attendance, quizzes, and certificates are included. Compare these features with the training tools you pay for today.

pillars.title: Spend less time chasing records
pillars.why: Reminders, assigned tasks, and overdue alerts help staff keep work moving. Managers can see who is responsible and which records still need attention.

pillars.title: Pennsylvania is built into the workflow
pillars.why: Chapters 2600 and 2800 have different requirements. CareBase tracks PCH and ALF training, resident assessments, support plans, and renewal dates in the context of your facility. Direct care training and separate dementia requirements stay distinct, with regulatory references available when you need the detail.
pillars.area: Rules and timing that reflect your setting

pillars.title: The next step stays connected to the record
pillars.why: A hospital return can open notification, reassessment, and support-plan review tasks. Completing training adds its attendance, hours, and certificate to the employee’s history. Owners and deadlines keep follow-up visible. Your survey binder draws on the records your team already maintains.

pillars.title: Training prepared for you. AI reviewed by people.
pillars.why: The CareMetric team uses your regulations, policies, or reference documents to draft courses with AI assistance. Drafts can include lesson text, video scripts, and graded quizzes; a reviewer checks the content and source references. Optional presenter videos can accompany the lessons. A named reviewer must approve the course before publication, and regenerating a section requires a new review.
pillars.area: Reviewed by a real person, every time

pillars.title: A price based on your facility, not your headcount
pillars.why: CareBase Core and its add-ons are flat-priced per facility, with unlimited residents and staff. Choose the modules you need: training, workforce, survey, eMAR, and billing. Training-only organizations can choose CareMetric Train with unlimited active learners. Start online, review your own workflows, and choose a paid plan when you are ready.

chapters.title: I run a personal care home
chapters.text: Your surveyor expects 12 hours of training a year per direct care worker (§2600.65, up to 6 on the job), current RASP assessments and support plans, medication practicums, Act 34 clearances, and fire drill logs — each documented and current. Completed training needs supporting records. CareBase keeps recorded hours, attendance, and certificates together for review.

chapters.title: I run an assisted living facility
chapters.text: Track 16 annual hours per direct care worker (§2800.65), separate dementia training (§2800.69), any additional special-care-unit training, and resident assessments and support plans (ASP). Each requirement has its own timing and documentation rules. Dementia training under §2800.69 does not count toward the 16-hour annual minimum. CareBase tracks those hours separately.

faq.question: What is CareMetric CareBase?
faq.answer: CareBase is software for staff training, resident records, daily operations, and survey preparation. It is designed primarily for Pennsylvania personal care homes and assisted living facilities. Teams share records in one system, with access based on each person’s role and assigned facilities.

faq.question: What can it replace?
faq.answer: Depending on your current tools, CareBase can replace separate training spreadsheets, attendance trackers, credential calendars, survey binders, basic staff schedules, incident logs, policy acknowledgment tools, and resident charge and payment ledgers. Compare the features with your existing workflows before retiring a tool.

faq.question: What does it not replace?
faq.answer: CareBase works alongside your electronic health record system, payroll, timeclock, HR system, accounting ledger, claims system, and emergency-call system. Compatible clinical systems can connect through FHIR, a healthcare data exchange standard. Keep using your existing medication administration record unless your facility completes enrollment, clinical approval, and a documented switch to CareBase’s native eMAR. Any required accredited or external training still needs to come from an eligible provider.

faq.question: Where do the savings come from?
faq.answer: Potential savings come from less duplicate entry, fewer manual reminders, quicker report preparation, and software you can stop paying for. Use the savings worksheet to estimate the value of time saved and software costs removed, using your own assumptions. It does not include savings from avoiding citations or other risks.

faq.question: Which regulations does it help with?
faq.answer: CareBase supports tracking under 55 Pa. Code Chapters 2600 (PCH) and 2800 (ALF), including staff training, resident assessments, support plans, administrator qualifications, medication practicums, fire drills, and incidents. Training workflows also support Chapter 6400 homes and federal aide requirements. Your team remains responsible for checking applicable rules and completing required official forms.

faq.question: Does it guarantee compliance or a deficiency-free survey?
faq.answer: No. CareBase helps your team track requirements, deadlines, responsibilities, and supporting records. Compliance and survey outcomes depend on accurate setup, qualified staff, completed work, and management follow-up.

faq.question: How many annual training hours does my provider type need?
faq.answer: Annual minimums depend on the facility type, role, and duties. PCH direct care workers generally need 12 hours; ALF direct care workers need 16. Chapter 6400 requires 24 hours for direct service workers, their supervisors, and program specialists, and 12 for specified other roles. Nurse aides, home health aides, and hospice aides generally need 12 hours. Additional dementia, specialty-unit, and practical training requirements may apply. See the guide for details and sources.

faq.question: Does it track resident-level compliance, not just staff?
faq.answer: Yes. For PCH and ALF facilities, CareBase tracks screening, assessments, reassessments, and support-plan updates. Deadlines differ by facility type and admission circumstances: for example, the PCH initial assessment is due within 15 days after admission, while the ALF assessment is generally due within the 30 days before admission. Specified ALF exceptions allow up to 15 days after admission. The required signed DHS form must still be retained.

faq.question: How does it track yearly in-service hours?
faq.answer: Administrators confirm employee duties and applicable requirements, then assign courses and deadlines. Completed courses, finalized class attendance, and approved outside training provide records for review. Pending or rejected outside training does not receive credit. Annual totals follow the applicable training period and eligibility rules.

faq.question: Do you support in-person, instructor-led training?
faq.answer: Yes. Trainers schedule classes, select employees for the roster, and mark who attended. They can print and upload a signed attendance sheet, confirm the training hours, and complete the class to create training records. Employees do not need to scan a code.

faq.question: Who reviews AI-generated training content?
faq.answer: A named human reviewer must approve AI-generated courses before publication. The CareMetric team drafts content from source documents, and the reviewer checks accuracy, completeness, and references. Regenerating a section requires a new review.

faq.question: What is the compliance copilot?
faq.answer: The compliance copilot helps answer questions about facility records and regulatory requirements, with references you can review. It can also draft proposed follow-up work. A person must review and approve an action before it is carried out; an answer or draft does not itself resolve a compliance gap.

faq.question: How are incidents, violations, and plans of correction handled?
faq.answer: Incident workflows track reporting tasks and deadlines for the relevant authorities and support report preparation. Staff must make and document the required reports. Access restrictions protect sensitive incidents. Violations and plans of correction have their own due dates and review steps so managers can track corrective work through verification.

faq.question: Can it schedule staff shifts too?
faq.answer: Yes. Set up units and shift types, record typical staff patterns, generate a draft schedule, and review it before publishing. Staff see published shifts in My Schedule. Cross-facility scheduling includes checks for overlapping assignments.

faq.question: Do you track background-check requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. CareBase tracks Act 34, 73, and 33 clearances, Older Adults Protective Services Act (OAPSA) provisional-employment deadlines, and documented suitability decisions. Federal exclusion-list checks, including OIG LEIE and SAM.gov, must be completed outside CareBase.

faq.question: Does CareBase keep a resident clinical record?
faq.answer: Yes. Staff can record vitals, progress notes, assessments, and care plans. Configured FHIR connections can import medications, allergies, and diagnoses from compatible systems. Imported medication events are read-only. Using CareBase’s native eMAR requires facility enrollment, clinical approval before use, and a documented switch to CareBase as the official medication administration record.

faq.question: Can one organization manage multiple facilities?
faq.answer: Yes. Organization administrators can review all facilities in their organization; facility managers are limited to their assigned sites. Reports follow the same access rules. Portfolio plans offer additional rollout support and reporting for larger operators.

faq.question: Can a state surveyor get read-only access?
faq.answer: Yes. Share a time-limited documentation room with only the records the surveyor requests. Surveyors never get a CareBase sign-in or edit access. Review the scope before sharing.

faq.question: Do employees need to install anything?
faq.answer: No installation is required to use CareBase in a supported browser. Employees can also add the training player to a phone’s home screen. Eligible downloaded training can be completed offline and synchronized when the device reconnects.

faq.question: Can staff get text or email reminders?
faq.answer: Yes. Configured reminders can notify staff about upcoming and overdue requirements by email and, when enabled, text message. Administrators can review unresolved alerts, weekly digests, and delivery status.

faq.question: Are there guest portals for families and admissions?
faq.answer: Yes. Time-limited links support move-in packages, resident-agreement signing, designated-person access, and documentation review. Guests can access the records shared with them without a full user account.

faq.question: What happens during an actual survey?
faq.answer: A manager can open Survey Day Mode to bring together the entrance-conference checklist, latest binder, on-shift staff roster, and prepared documentation rooms. Staff use those records to respond to requests and record what has been provided. Any cited violations can then be entered into the plan-of-correction workflow.

faq.question: What if my administrator quits?
faq.answer: Your organization retains its requirements, records, deadlines, and history. An authorized administrator can update access and assign responsibilities so the next administrator can continue the work. Keep organization contacts and account permissions current during the transition.

faq.question: Can I cancel and keep my records?
faq.answer: Yes. Your organization owns its records and can export them during the wind-down period after cancellation. Review the retention and export terms before closing the account.

faq.question: Is CareBase easy for staff to use?
faq.answer: Staff have focused screens for their assignments, schedule, and records. For classes, the trainer records attendance on the roster, or staff can use a shared kiosk with a name and PIN. Training is available in a browser. Use the trial to check whether these workflows work well for your team.

faq.question: Can a new organization start immediately?
faq.answer: You can begin signup online on your own. Enter your organization details, verify your email, and set a password, then import staff and configure requirements during the free trial.

faq.question: Can we bring over our existing roster?
faq.answer: Yes. Upload a CSV staff roster, review the import preview, and resolve any flagged entries before applying it. You can also add employees individually.
